title: The yield strength of a body when its shape was set, by material, and how the materials mix (GEN.1158, physics/roundness.py)
note: This file is where measured strengths drop in. Every number here is a stand-in (registry rows RN1 to RN7, section 6.126 of the gap filling plan); a material gives either 'strength_pa' (a strength at the scale of a body, Pa) or 'round_radius_km' with 'reference_density_kg_m3' (the mean radius at which bodies of that material and density were seen to turn round; the strength that rounds a body at that size is worked out from it). 'same_as' gives a material the strength of another until it has its own. 'mixing', 'porosity' and 'temperature' each name a rule of physics/roundness.py (MIXING_RULES, POROSITY_RULES, TEMPERATURE_RULES) and its numbers. A new rule is one function and one name; the engine's interface (ice fraction, metal fraction, porosity and a shape-set temperature in; strength, round radius, roundness ratio out) does not change. Values follow /mnt/project-files/reports/planetary-material-strength-2026-10-31.md, section 7 and section 11.

ice.label: water ice and the other ices of an icy moon, at the strength of ice near 160 K (the default when no shape-set temperature is given)
ice.source: Lineweaver and Norman 2010 (arXiv:1004.1091) fit of 0.4 to 3 MPa; equals the Durham, Kirby and Stern 1997 creep strength of pure ice near 158 K at 1e-15 per second (strength research section 11a)

rock.label: silicate rock of an asteroid or rocky moon
rock.source: Lineweaver and Norman 2010 (arXiv:1004.1091) Fig. 2: Pallas 275 km and Vesta 265 km round, Juno 115 km not; confirmed three ways in strength research section 6 (range 4 to 30 MPa)

metal.label: iron and nickel metal
metal.source: Pohl and Britt 2020 iron meteorite lab yield 320 to 450 MPa and kamacite single crystal 134 MPa at 300 K, divided by 2 to 6 for inclusions and cracks (strength research section 5)

mixing.source: strength of ice with hard grains = ice strength x exp(2 x grain volume fraction), measured to 0.56 (Durham et al. 1992 as printed in Durham, Kirby and Stern 1997 eq. 3); continued to 0.65 (random close packing, recalled) then geometric to the solids' strength at 1 (an extrapolation of the strength research)

porosity.source: off: Pohl and Britt 2020 find no clear strength trend with porosity in meteorites. 'exponential' (strength x exp(-b x porosity), b 4 to 7, a ceramics-based recalled placeholder, 'coefficient' here) is built and not used; it would make Proteus round

temperature.source: Durham, Kirby and Stern 1997 (JGR 102:16293) Table 2, dislocation creep of pure ice I (grain size 0.6 to 1 mm); strain rate = A sigma^n exp(-E / RT); the weakest regime governs; the pressure term is dropped (small bodies); an upper bound at the lowest stresses. Rate 1e-15 per second is a tunable stand-in (strength research section 11a)
